premises: Go heap: a list of backing arrays (byte values as Nat). A slice is (backing, offset, len, cap); append writes in place when len + k <= cap, else allocates a new backing array.

Oracle (Go 1.24 runtime, runtime/slice.go nextslicecap + roundupsize for noscan byte slices): new capacity = smallest size class >= nextslicecap(newLen, oldCap). The class table (runtime/sizeclasses.go class_to_size) is in the state, truncated to classes <= 512 bytes: larger allocations are out of scope (the model then uses the exact requested capacity, which is wrong for real Go). The search policy keeps every slice below 512 bytes.
NewBatchData's make([]byte, 0) slices have capacity 0 and no backing array (backing index 0 is never written while cap = 0).
l1TxHashes, blockNum and l1TxNum are not modelled (no aliasing relevant to TxsPayloadV2).
